# Journal — job S1b (WebKit 5.12.0, theme 5.2.2, icons 4.4.0)

- 14:51 Started. Read BRIEF, pages.json. Scaffolded Vite vue-ts app, installed the three tarballs + vue-router.
- 14:51 **low** — `webkit init -y` worked well: wrote webkit.css, eslint/stylelint config, .claude rules/skills, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, patched main.ts, added tailwind v4 + postcss devDeps. It added `"prepare": "husky"` and husky without asking (side effect on a fresh repo). It notes "defaults to LIGHT, set data-theme=dark" — good, clear.
- 14:51 **medium (doc oddity)** — The package ships `docs/reviews/m2.7/battery-2-kit/` including `structure/site-solution-*.txt`: the server-rendered component trees of exactly these pages (block-hero-title-band, block-capability-grid, block-media-split-stack-solutions, block-client-quotes, block-platform-directory, block-network-section, block-recognition-marquee, block-faq-section, block-closing-call-to-action-split). Very useful as a map, but it is evaluation/review material shipped in the npm tarball (also owner-feedback PNGs) — bloats the package and is not user documentation. I used it as the section→component map.
- 14:55 **high** — TypeScript: `vue-tsc -b` (the default `npm run build` of a vue-ts Vite app) fails with TS2307 "Cannot find module '@aziontech/webkit/hero-band'" for EVERY component import. The exports map points straight at `.vue` source files (`./src/components/sections/hero-band/hero-band.vue`), which TS's `moduleResolution: bundler` cannot resolve through package exports. README claims "`vue-tsc --noEmit` checks it under strict" and only mentions the `htmlAttributes` option — not true for a fresh `npm create vite` vue-ts project. Also TS 6.0 (what create-vite now installs) breaks the `@aziontech/icons` side-effect import (TS2882); downgraded to TS 5.9. Workaround: `src/webkit-shims.d.ts` declaring `@aziontech/webkit/*` as DefineComponent and `@aziontech/webkit/assets/*` as string — loses all prop typing. ~10 min.
- 14:55 **medium** — Doc examples for logo/illustration props (NetworkSection, RecognitionMarquee, ClientQuotes, MediaSplitStack, ComplianceBadges…) use public URLs like `/marketing-components/logos/dafiti-extended-mono.svg` that do not exist in a consumer app. Only `src/assets/site-assets.json` (undocumented) reveals the mapping to the exported `@aziontech/webkit/assets/<file>.svg` subpaths. I import those (Vite turns them into URLs). No doc says how a consumer should serve them.
- 14:55 **low (worked well)** — The solution-page template maps almost 1:1 onto section components: HeroBand(title-band), CapabilityGrid, MediaSplitStack, TemplateGallery, ClientQuotes, PlatformDirectory, NetworkSection, RecognitionMarquee, FaqSection, ClosingCallToAction(split), plus SiteNav/SiteFooter and SectionContainer/SectionGap. Props tables in llms/components/*.md are clear.
- 14:56 **medium** — `webkit init` wires a husky pre-commit running `npx eslint .`, but the generated `eslint.config.mjs` has no `ignores` for `dist/`: after the first `npm run build` every commit fails with ~49 `webkit/no-hardcoded-color` errors inside WebKit's own bundled code (`dist/assets/scene-*.js`, index-*.js). Added `{ ignores: ['dist/**'] }`. The stock create-vite `vite.config.ts` comment also fails `webkit/authoring-standards` (prose-comment) — harsh for a config file. ~5 min.
- 14:56 **medium** — `webkit check` [imports] flags `declare module '@aziontech/webkit/*'` in a .d.ts as "not exported" (false positive on a type shim). Had to replace the wildcard shim with one generated `declare module` per used subpath (types/webkit-shims.d.ts). Also: `check` printed no [lint] section at all, so I ran eslint/stylelint myself.
- 14:56 **low** — `webkit check` doctor warned "no WebkitProvider in src/"; nothing in the website shell block or SiteNav docs mentions it. Added `<WebkitProvider locale="en">` at the app root.
- 14:56 **medium** — Overline blinking cursor (HeroBand eyebrow, SectionTitle eyebrows, ClosingCallToAction eyebrow) is painted with `bg-(--accent)`, and `--accent` is #0072F5 (blue) in theme 5.2.2 dark. The site reference has an orange cursor / orange '//' system. No prop to change it; not restyling. Visible blue bar next to every eyebrow.

WebKit ships those as `Diagram` names ('cache', 'load-balancer', 'image-processor', …) but MediaSplitStack cannot take a diagram/scene (MediaSplitBand takes `scene`, but is a different framed layout without the sticky stack). # DONE — job S1b

## Pages
- `site-solution-performance`: built — all 11 template bands (hero, 3×2 capability grid, 4 media-split bands, client quotes + logo tabs, platform directory, network map + 4 client outcomes, recognition marquee, FAQ, split closing CTA) plus SiteNav/SiteFooter. Gaps: band media are WebKit illustrations, not the reference's request-flow diagrams; blue (not orange) eyebrow cursor; Rubik instead of the site's heading face; FAQ answers written by me (reference only gives questions).
- `site-solution-ai`: built — same, plus TemplateGallery (6 templates, stack ticker) and the benefit-style network floor. Same gaps.
- `site-solution-security`: built — same template, 4 bands, benefit network floor. Same gaps.
- `site-solution-streaming`: built — same template, 2 bands, client outcomes floor. Same gaps.
- `/` lists links to all four pages.

## WebKit pieces used most
SectionContainer (site) + SectionGap (hatch), HeroBand (title-band, large), CapabilityGrid, MediaSplitStack, TemplateGallery, ClientQuotes, PlatformDirectory, NetworkSection (outcomes), RecognitionMarquee, FaqSection, ClosingCallToAction (split), SiteNav, SiteFooter, WebkitProvider, Link/SectionTitle (index page), `@aziontech/webkit/assets/*` logos, brand-mark and illustration registries, `ai`/`pi` icon fonts.

## Top 5 problems with WebKit (by impact)
1. **TypeScript doesn't work out of the box (high):** every `@aziontech/webkit/<name>` import fails `vue-tsc -b` (TS2307) because the exports map points at raw `.vue` files; TS 6 also rejects the `@aziontech/icons` side-effect import. Needed TS 5.9 and a hand-generated per-module `declare module` shim, so components lose their prop types. And `webkit check` flags a wildcard shim as an unknown import.
2. **Media splits can't show diagrams (medium):** MediaSplitStack takes only `image`/`illustration`. The reference bands show the product request-flow diagrams that WebKit ships as `Diagram` specs, so every page shows the wrong kind of picture.
3. **Theme mismatches the site (medium):** `--font-sans` is Rubik, not the site's heading face, so headings wrap differently. The Overline cursor uses `--accent`, which is blue (#0072F5), not the orange the site uses. Neither can change without overriding tokens.
4. **Tooling side effects (medium):** `init` adds a husky pre-commit hook, but its ESLint/Stylelint config doesn't ignore `dist/`. After the first build, every commit fails on WebKit's own bundled hex colours. The stock create-vite comment also fails `authoring-standards`. `webkit check` printed no lint section.
5. **Doc examples use asset URLs that don't exist (medium):** examples use `/marketing-components/...` paths a consumer app doesn't have. The mapping to the exported `@aziontech/webkit/assets/*.svg` files is only in an undocumented `site-assets.json`. Smaller gaps: ClientQuotes autoplays with no prop to control it; SiteNav shows Login on mobile; SiteFooter has no external-link flag; NetworkSection's benefits floor had to be faked with logo-less outcomes. Also, the package ships review/eval material (`docs/reviews/m2.7/battery-2-kit`).

## Build
`npm run build` (vue-tsc -b && vite build) **passes**. `webkit check`: 0 errors, 1 warning. eslint and stylelint are clean. `dist/` works as a static SPA (tested with `vite preview`: unknown paths return index.html). Git history: setup commit, then one commit per page.
